reasons.emulator:
VERIFIED 2026-06-01: ExtremeXOS 21.1 boots with IDE bus (hda.qcow2).
Despite vendor docs saying sata, the kernel mounts /dev/hda* → must use ide.
reasons.console:
NPX-821 (Wave 21 U3): console changed telnet -> vnc. ExtremeXOS never writes a
login prompt to the serial port; it is a framebuffer-console guest. Measured on
this host 2026-09-05 by booting the shipped images in an isolated scratchpad QEMU
that mirrors the pre-libvirt-lanes raw-QEMU argv (NPX-825 PR2 later replaced that launch path with libvirt lanes; this comment describes the 2026-09-05 probe as it was actually run), across five variants (21.1.1.4 and 15.3.2 x
QEMU 4.1.0/2.12.0 x -cpu host/Nehalem x 512/2048 MB x with/without a VGA device
x with/without NICs). In every single run:
* the GRUB entry the image auto-selects is literally titled ".. using VGA
console", and the kernel cmdline it builds ends "console=tty0" with "quiet";
the LAST console= on a Linux cmdline is the one that becomes /dev/console, so
userland's stdout goes to the framebuffer, and "quiet" drops everything below
KERN_ERR from the serial port too;
* userland output is visible ON SCREEN (e.g. "ifconfig: ioctl 0x8913 failed: No
such device") while the serial log holds exactly 1 byte - 0xff, which is
QEMU's own telnet IAC negotiation, i.e. ZERO bytes from the guest.
Removing the VGA card (-vga none) does not redirect anything to serial; it only
blinds the guest (the hypothesis that -nographic drops the VGA device was tested
and is false: qtree shows the VGA present under both -nographic and -vga std).
So a "telnet" console here promised a text console that cannot exist, and both
config doors then tried to converse with silence. With console: "vnc" the user
gets the working screen, and refuse_if_no_config_channel() answers
GraphicalConsoleOnly - whose message ("a serial port IS attached and reachable,
the guest just never writes to it") is a verbatim description of what was
measured. This is why the wave classes these images B (graphical), not A or D.
